abstract: We investigate whether the definition of economic rationality as choice consistency is correlated with decision-making ability. Guided by a theoretical framework, we demonstrate that documented positive correlations may be driven by confounding properties unrelated to consistency. To address this, in a novel experiment, we isolate consistency, measured by the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference. We show that less sophisticated decision-makers often rely on simple rules and behave consistently, while more sophisticated ones consciously randomize, appearing inconsistent. These patterns determine ambiguous correlations, raising doubts about the choice of language that equates consistency with rationality in economics. Similar content being viewed by others
abstract_zh: 我们探究了将经济理性定义为选择一致性是否与决策能力相关。在理论框架的指导下，我们证明已有文献中记录的正相关关系可能由与一致性无关的混淆属性驱动。为此，在一项新颖的实验中，我们通过显示偏好弱公理来分离一致性。研究表明，决策能力较弱的个体往往依赖简单规则并表现出一致性行为，而决策能力较强的个体则会有意识地随机化选择，从而显得不一致。这些模式决定了模糊的相关性，对经济学中将一致性等同于理性的语言选择提出了质疑。
title: On the relation between rationality and consistency
title_zh: 论理性与一致性之间的关系

abstract: We study changes in markups across 70 product markets from 2006 to 2018. A growing literature has documented rising markups using a production function approach. We instead estimate demand and invert firms’ first-order pricing conditions to infer markups. To make the method scalable, we propose estimating nested logit demand models using household panel data to automate the assignment of products to nests. We find an overall upward trend in markups, with considerable heterogeneity across and within product markets. These increases are primarily driven by changes in firms’ marginal costs and households’ price sensitivity instead of changes in firm ownership.
title: Scalable Demand and Markups
title_zh: 可扩展需求与加成定价

abstract: We develop a Bayesian Wald-type test for detecting temporal differences in connectedness from variance decompositions, and establish the asymptotic normality of impulse response functions and variance decomposition matrices at fixed local time points. The resulting test statistic is asymptotically χ 2 distributed under the null hypothesis and performs well in Monte Carlo simulations. Applying our methodology to high-frequency options data on sectoral exchange-traded funds (ETFs) from January 2013 to June 2023, we identify and quantify monetary policy surprises following Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcements. Our empirical results indicate that total connectedness among sectoral ETF implied volatilities increases significantly following FOMC announcements, with these elevated connectedness levels persisting for approximately one hour on days with monetary policy surprises. Our findings indicate more than one-fifth of FOMC announcements surprise financial markets.
title: Testing for differences in high-frequency network connectedness from variance decompositions
title_zh: 基于方差分解的高频网络连通性差异检验

abstract: Abstract One of the most contentious issues in the study of the Atlantic slave trade is the profitability of the trade. In this paper, we contribute by pooling all available data on transatlantic slave ship voyage accounts into a joint dataset. This dataset includes data from a period of 100 years (1730–1830) and from five nations (Denmark, France, Great Britain, the Netherlands, and Spain). It permits calculation of the trade's profitability (total net returns over net outlays). Using weight calibration sampling methods, we compute a representative profit rate between 1750 and 1795 for France, Great Britain, and the Netherlands. Our results suggest that the average profitability (net returns over net outlay) was not remarkably high (around 11–14 per cent for multi‐year ventures), with a very high variance. Some observations allow the computation of internal rates of return, which we then apply to the rest of the dataset. This shows that profits were low compared with alternative investment opportunities.
title: Benefitting from brutality? Profits of north‐western Europe's slave trade at the eve of the industrial revolution
title_zh: 从残暴中获益？工业革命前夕西北欧奴隶贸易的利润

abstract: We examine the health effects of a labor market activation policy in Sweden, the Youth Job Guarantee. To estimate causal effects, we implement a regression discontinuity design using the policy's age-eligibility threshold, together with detailed administrative data on health-related outcomes, including indicators of mental health. Health effects could arise indirectly, via effects on employment, or directly, for example via improved daily routines. In contrast to most existing studies on the health effects of active labor market programs, our results indicate that the activation policy did not have clear positive effects on health one year after the start of unemployment, measured by prescribed medication or medical contacts.
title: Health effects of a youth labor market activation policy
title_zh: 青年劳动力市场激活政策的健康效应

abstract: We introduce a novel method to quantify perceived global risk and ambiguity in media attention using content analysis. First, we apply structural topic modeling to risk-related news articles to identify distinct sources of uncertainty. We define ambiguity in attention as the variability in the distribution of topic probabilities across articles—that is, the extent to which media coverage diverges in its focus on different topics. In contrast, perceived risk is measured as the share of articles that assign a particular topic as their primary focus. We then examine whether these measures of perceived global risk and ambiguity in attention can explain changes in credit default swap (CDS) spreads. Our results show that greater ambiguity in news media attention is associated with a decrease in CDS spreads by up to 5.9%, while higher perceived risk corresponds to an increase of up to 4.9%. These findings highlight the role of media-driven uncertainty in shaping investor behavior and market risk perceptions.
journal: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
title: Decoding news: How media risk and ambiguity shape CDS spreads
title_zh: 解读新闻：媒体风险与模糊性如何影响信用违约互换利差
